summary: Tested iter41 — (a) inline Tier-3 progressive-disclosure prompts wired into Budget Calculator, Contribution Estimator, Reassessment Letter, Statement Decoder, and (b) deep-link onboarding via /onboarding?pid=<id>. Backend: ran 19 existing tests (all pass) + wrote 7 new tests in test_iter41_inline_prompts.py covering all 4 prompt-routing slugs, save-then-disappear behaviour, full-profile empty prompts, and PATCH-no-duplicate (all 7 pass — 26/26 backend). Frontend Playwright: verified anonymous users see no panel, budget_calculator panel renders with all 5 supplements + conditional enteral bolus/non_bolus testids + save flow, contribution_estimator renders both NumberPct editors and save removes prompt, dashboard CTA href = /onboarding?pid=<uuid>, and the deep-link onboarding mode pre-fills Tier 1 fields (first/last name, DOB, pension status) and shows the onboarding-complete-now-banner.

issues: React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' in ce-class / rl-class <select> options. Caused by the dev-mode source-injection wrapper but worth confirming it doesn't ship to production bundle.

critical_code_review_comments: ProfileInlinePrompts.load() catches all errors silently (line ~39-41). Good for unauthenticated UX but masks real backend faults from logs — consider narrowing the catch to 401/403.

_build_profile_prompts in participant_profile.py emits BOTH a reassessment_letter and a statement_decoder prompt for the same care_manager_name field. After save the user sees a 'Saved' toast in one tool but the prompt for the same field reappears if they navigate to the other tool (until they refresh — load() will pick it up). This is by design (two distinct UX surfaces) but worth documenting.
Onboarding.jsx is now ~860 lines including ProfileCompletionBanner — overdue for splitting into step files (Step1Essentials.jsx, Step2Authorisation.jsx, Step3Recommended.jsx, Step4Done.jsx).

Deep-link mode (editPid) PATCHes the existing participant on Step 2. There is no guard against a malicious user pasting another account's pid into the URL — server correctly 404s via account_id scoping in patch_participant, so safe; but the UI shows a brief loader/error which could be friendlier.
